newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian Metals - Chinese in small-lot copper buying.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - Chinese in small-lot copper buying.

text.p: Chinese buyers have been seen picking up a few thousand tonnes of copper over the past week to take advantage of the recent fall in prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said on Friday.
"The Chinese bought something. Prices have dropped so they're taking advantage," a dealer for a European firm said.
"I think the Chinese will lift 5,000 tonnes of copper," the general manager of a Japanese metal dealing firm said. "We've also received inquiries from India."
Chinese buyers are thought to be behind the decline in copper stocks in the LME warehouse in Singapore since mid-March.
The volume of copper in the LME's warehouse here reached 29,300 tonnes in the exchange's stocks report on Thursday against the 55,000 tonnes reported on March 14.
Several traders said, however, that China may put off any large scale buying until next week on expectations that LME copper prices may head further south.
Three month copper was quoted by Far East dealers at 0600 GMT at around US$2,304/09 a tonne against the close in London on Thursday at $2,306.
"The market is bearish. I think the Chinese are just checking prices. We may see them more in the market early next week," one trader said.
"It's down, down, down," a Singapore dealer said. "(Three month) copper's support should be around US$2,275/85 (a tonne)."
"There's no factor to push prices up," another added.

Metal brokers Brandeis said in its daily review that the stalemate between Phelps Dodge Corp and its workers at the Chino, New Mexico plant "could well support the downside to (copper) prices as strike concerns remain."
"Technically, (the market) has again stalled above $2,300 and could return to $2,280 to confirm downside support," Brandeis said.

Zinc dealers, on the other hand, welcomed the recent correction in LME prices. Zinc had touched 4-1/2 year highs last month above $1,300 a tonne before ending on Thursday $22 down on the day at $1,244 a tonne.
"I think it's pretty healthy to have a correction," one senior trader said, adding he still sees a tight supply crunch for zinc developing in the second half of the year.
"Good support is now seen in the $1,220 range," Brandeis said.
Around 7,000 tonnes of zinc from China was said to have been placed on LME warrant Singapore and a few thousand more remain off warrant, dealers said.
Another 2,000-3,000 tonnes of zinc may arrive in Singapore from the same destination in the next few weeks.
The material being shipped to Singapore, though, is easily offset by the fact "that stocks of zinc in other LME warehouses are regularly coming down," one trader said.
Trading in the rest of the base metal complex in Asia was quiet with many buyers sitting on the sidelines.
"Sentiment is pretty weak," one dealer said.
